description: One resonant band-pass filter of the kind Rainbow carries six of, with an envelope follower beside it

params.text: Sets the resonance, from a wide noisy band at the bottom to a narrow ringing sine at the top
Sets the filter frequency a volt per octave, ten octaves either side of C4 at 261.63Hz
Chooses the filter: 1P is the one-pass MaxQ filter and 2P the two-pass
Sets what the envelope output carries: a fast follower, a slow follower, or a trigger
Nothing in the module reads this switch: the noise it chooses is used only while the audio input is empty, and with that jack empty the module stops working altogether
Attenuates the frequency CV, from none of it at the bottom to all of it at the top
Attenuates the Q CV, from none of it at the bottom to all of it at the top

inputs.text: Raises the resonance, through its own attenuator, 10V for the whole range; a negative voltage does nothing
Shifts the filter frequency a volt per octave through its own attenuator, added to the frequency knob and held within ten octaves either side of C4

outputs.text: An envelope following the filter's output, 0 to 10V

notes: the module does nothing at all until a cable is in the audio input: with that jack empty it stops processing, and both outputs hold the last voltage they were given
bypassing the module passes the audio input straight to the audio output

inputs.0:
0 to 10V · continuous · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.1:
1V per octave · continuous · one channel only

the knob and this input are summed and the total held to ±10V.
inputs.2:
continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads nothing; the module stops processing.
